name: The Middle Watch
summary: The North Atlantic, the small hours of 1 September 1985: you're on the logbook in the Argo control van aboard R/V Knorr, sorting what a camera sled sees on the seafloor two and a half miles down. Freeze, print, pin, log: rock, life, junk, and an empty column marked '?'. Then a boiler with three furnace doors turns up on the screen, and at 2:20 a.m. everyone goes out on the fantail and stands quietly over the cable.
motifs: monitor as a window into a second world
the tow cable into black water
thread: On the middle watch aboard R/V Knorr, 1 September 1985, the player sorted the seafloor still by still until a riveted boiler came up on the Argo monitor. They matched it to a 1911 plate, crossed out the '?' on the board and wrote TITANIC, and phoned the galley to wake the chief. The van cheered, then fell silent when the clock reached 2:20, the hour she sank, and the watch stood on the fantail over the tow cable. The player followed the cable down. Carried: a warm thermal print of the boiler, round-faced with three shut furnace doors, stamped 01:05. Still open: what you owe a thing you wanted so badly to find, once you've found it.
delight: I loved that an epic search for the most famous wreck in the world comes down to a tired person holding a curl of warm printer paper and asking 'is this a rock?' a hundred times. The board labelled in marker, Gerald the rattail fish, and a dropstone an iceberg let go of all felt true, and the strike through the '?' felt like the hinge of the whole thing. Then the clock says 02:14 and the cheering just stops.

idea.name: The Middle Watch
idea.premise: North Atlantic, the night the Titanic was found in 1985. In the dark Argo control van aboard R/V Knorr, the watch freezes, prints, pins and logs every contact a towed camera sled finds on the seabed, sorting the deep into ROCK, LIFE, JUNK and an empty '?'. Weeks of wanting come down to a boiler with three furnace doors, a cheer, and a minute's silence at 2:20 a.m. over the cable that runs down to her.
